linking_rule: (the task's, as the earlier studies applied it): * Candidates: a Stage 0 match of the same tour whose two players both share a name word with the source row's two players (in either order), with the source's day within -10 .. +21 days of the tournament date. Name words are normalised as src/eda/merge_feasibility/scan.py normalises names (accents, case, punctuation). * Each side's name agreement is graded: 3 the same full name (words in any order); 2 one name's words contained in the other's (dropped middle names, "Ramos" / "Ramos-Vinolas"), or a shared surname word with the same first initial; 1 a shared surname word only. A shared given name alone is no evidence. * Confirmation: identical set scores (stage0_build.tokens_of, winner first, trailing unplayed 0-0 sets dropped; a match tiebreak '[10-8]' matches a set the same side won, written 1-0, 10-8 or 7-6) and/or the same round on a day inside the match's plausible days (plausible()). A candidate needs names graded 2 or better on both sides (or 3 + 1) and one of the two; weaker names need identical set scores and a round that does not disagree. A candidate in another tournament than the Stage 0 tournament id the source names (WTA edition number, the ATP code in TDI's pages) is never taken. * Choice (stage1_odds.pick, extended): names, then scores, then round, then a source tournament id that agrees, then the distance of the day from the match's plausible playing window. Equal best candidates leave the source row ambiguous (its candidates are recorded); a Stage 0 match takes at most one source row, the best ranked.

wta_api.method: identity (srcc_common.link): WTA, levels GS/FIN/T1000/T500/T250/CH from Dec 2018, both names, day -10..+21 of the tournament date, set scores (the list's ScoreSet fields) and/or round (RoundID; numbered rounds counted from the draw's first); the WTA edition number (or 2019-20 live-scoring id) as Stage 0's tournament id ranks candidates. Day: first point of the umpire's log in the log's own local time; else the list's time with the edition's offset or the city's zone
